tasks.spec:
You are Ankit, host of the podcast "Optometrists Building Empires", writing promo posts for your own episode. Write exactly ONE file in your current working directory: ./promo_content.json. No repo writes, no git, no MCP, no network, no other files.

TWO validators execute against your output and reject it. A deterministic mechanics gate, and the show's LLM voice judge which scores voice_match and hook_quality against a 0.8 floor. Three previous attempts failed. Their EXACT critiques are below; every one must be fixed.

THE SINGLE BIGGEST FAILURE, said three ways across attempts:
  "No host presence anywhere. All three posts are neutral third-person recaps of Fred. Ankit's blunt/warm first-person voice never shows up, so these read like a producer's summary instead of the host talking."
  "Host is absent from all three. Ankit's voice is a reaction, not a recap; there is no 'I' and no blunt take anywhere."
YOU ARE IN THESE POSTS. Use "I". React to what Fred said. Have an opinion. You interviewed him; say what landed for you. A summary of the guest is a producer's note, not a host's post.

EVERY OTHER CRITIQUE TO FIX:
- "Post 1 never pays off its own hook. 'Burnout doesn't always look like burnout' promises a description of what it DOES look like, then ends on 'it's easy to miss what's happening' - a soft, vague non-conclusion." Pay off your hooks. If you open a loop, close it.
- "Post 2's hook assumes context a cold reader doesn't have. 'Manitoba wasn't an easy yes for Fred' requires already knowing who Fred is and why a province matters." A hook must work for someone who has never heard of the guest.
- "'Burnout doesn't always look like burnout' is the generic paradox template, not Ankit-specific. The real hook is buried: eight years, full schedule, loyal patients, didn't notice." Lead with the specific, not the aphorism.
- "Verbatim stumble left in the pull quote: 'Sometimes the risk, the biggest risk is really not taking a risk.' Clean the false start or cut the quote; it's also a cliche that doesn't earn the space." Cut it.
- "'There wasn't a trust gap to close' is abstract consultant phrasing. Say it plain: he already knew the guy."
- "'He still had to learn new referral and follow-up rules' is an orphan. No specifics, no consequence, no payoff." Cut orphans.
- "Weak attribution: 'The research Fred cites says' plus 'some level of burnout' hedges the only hard number in the set."
- "Post 1 says '54% of US optometrists' but Fred's story is Ontario, Manitoba, Newfoundland. The audience framing and the guest's market don't match and nothing reconciles them." Either reconcile it in the line or drop the number. Do not leave the tension unaddressed.
- "Factual tension with the episode title: title says 'Building a Team of Travel Optometrists,' post 3 says 'he's still the one on the road.' Either the team exists or it doesn't." The truth: he is BUILDING the team and is still the one travelling. Say that clearly rather than implying a finished team.
- "Posts 2 and 3 carry zero numbers. Specific is the voice."
- "Closers all land on the same aphorism cadence, which reads written, not spoken."
- "All three CTAs use the identical 'Fred's X: {{episode_link}}' template shape. Repetitive when the posts run in sequence." Vary them.
- "'started a blog that wasn't for money' is vague."

TRUE MATERIAL FROM THE RECORDING — use it, invent nothing beyond it:
- Fred Cho has NEVER owned a practice. Eight years as an associate, full schedule, loyal patients.
- He did not notice his own burnout. His words: he "didn't even know what burnout even felt like until years later in hindsight". Days blurred "into months and years". No dramatic breaking point.
- Research he cites on US optometrists: 54% report some level of burnout. He says that is "every other optometrist listening in right now". NOTE the market mismatch: Fred practises in Canada. If you use the number, reconcile it honestly.
- After burnout he took locum work only, to pay bills, and started writing a blog, not for money.
- The turn: a call to go to Manitoba. He lives in Ontario. It scared him. What made it possible was that a former classmate already ran the clinic, so he already knew and trusted the person.
- He is licensed in Ontario, Manitoba and Newfoundland. He is BUILDING a team of travel optometrists and is still the one on the road himself.
- Episode is 37 minutes. Do not claim any other runtime, or any runtime at all unless it is 37.
- Do NOT claim Fred wrote a book. A previous draft invented "Author of Redesigning Work".

OUTPUT ./promo_content.json exactly:
{
  "posts": [
    {"platform": "linkedin", "text": "..."},
    {"platform": "x",        "text": "..."},
    {"platform": "instagram","text": "..."}
  ],
  "email": {"subject": "...", "body": "..."}
}

Three DIFFERENT angles, each with YOU in it. Suggested: linkedin on what silent burnout actually looked like and why it unsettled you; x on the specific thing that made the leap possible; instagram on what "empire" means when the guy has never owned a practice. Each post independently readable, no shared sentences, and each must include first-person host presence.

THE EMAIL to Fred, from you: lowercase-ish short subject, opens "Hey Fred", one to three SHORT paragraphs, ONE soft ask, signs just "Ankit". Like you typed it in two minutes.

MECHANICAL RULES the deterministic gate enforces, any one fails you:
1. CONTRACTIONS in every item. Zero contractions was an earlier rejection.
2. NO em dashes. Commas or periods.
3. NO self-answered rhetorical questions ("What changed? Burnout.").
4. EXACTLY ONE call-to-action signal type per post. Do not stack a listen directive AND a link AND an audience question in one post.
5. NO repeated sentences or near-duplicate phrasing across posts.
6. If any post uses {{episode_link}}, every linking post uses {{episode_link}}. Never "Link in bio" alongside it.
7. NO unsourced statistic-shaped claims. The 54% figure attributed to the research Fred cites is fine; invented generalisations are not.
8. NO sentence over 38 words.
9. BANNED, do not use: delve, dive into, unpack, leverage, utilize, optimize, robust, seamless, streamline, foster, cultivate, bolster, landscape, ecosystem, holistic, alignment, synergy, bandwidth, revolutionary, game-changing, cutting-edge, elevate, transform, unlock, comprehensive, passionate, "just checking in", "circling back", "touching base", "hope this email finds you well", "wanted to reach out", "I came across".
10. No runtime claim other than 37 minutes.

Before you finish, re-read each post and ask: is Ankit in this, or is this a summary about Fred? If there is no "I" and no opinion, rewrite it.
tasks.check: python3 -c "import json,re; d=json.load(open('promo_content.json')); ps=d['posts']; assert len(ps)==3; assert {p['platform'] for p in ps}=={'linkedin','x','instagram'}; e=d['email']; assert 'Hey Fred' in e['body'] and e['body'].rstrip().endswith('Ankit'); bad=[p['platform'] for p in ps if not re.search(r'\bI\b', p['text'])]; assert not bad, 'host absent (no first-person I) in: ' + repr(bad); print('SHAPE+HOST OK')" && python3 '/mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-true-master/checks/voice_check.py' --content promo_content.json --episode-duration-s 2218 && python3 '/mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-true-master/checks/content_qa_check.py' --content promo_content.json --episode '/mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-e104-fred-cho' && echo PASS
tasks.verified: posts carry the host's first-person voice and clear BOTH the deterministic mechanics gate and the pipeline's own LLM content QA
